newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares end up on easing inflation forecast.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares end up on easing inflation forecast.

text.p: Greek stocks ended 3.36 percent higher on heavy volume with banking shares leading the rally and market watchers saying there was a positive sentiment in the Greek bourse on easing February inflation estimates.

"There was a strong buying interest on Thursday across the board. Market sentiment is optimistic on expectations of a lower rate of inflation in February," said Vassilis Gianniadis, a floor trader at M. Kyranis Securities.
He said the market expected February inflation to fall to 6.5-6.6 percent from 6.8 percent in January.
"Because of the recent steep fall of the index, people felt less confident in the market. However, they were returning because fixed income returns were not that appealing," he said.
He added that the political crisis in neighbouring Albania did not affect the Greek bourse on Thursday.
The crisis started deteriorating on Wednesday when heavily armed insurgents set up defence lines at the entrance of the town of Sarande, ready to fight with the Albanian army.
Another analyst said the rise was a justified reaction to the market's recent fall.

"Thursday's rise was expected after such a steep drop. We had been expecting a correction anyway, but at a milder pace. The market is now rebounding," said Evelyn Vougesi, an analyst at Kyklos Securities.

Expectations that Athens will be among the four or five candidate cities to host the Olympic Games of 2004 when the IOC announces its shortlist on Friday, construction shares gained another 4.51 percent on Thursday.
Athens, along with Rome and Stockholm were regarded as having the strongest technical bids.
Gianniadis said Friday would be an important day for the Greek bourse and the constructions sector.

The Athens general share index ended 3.36 percent or 43.43 points higher at 1335.60 points from Wednesday's 1292.17, after opening at 1300.41. The session's high was at 1348.07 points and its low at 1300.41.
Turnover was 26.9 billion drachmas on volume of 7.1 million shares. There were several block trades during the session. Advancers led decliners 178 to 45 with 28 issues unchanged on 251 traded.
Banking shares ended 5.16 percent higher, leading the rally. Investment stocks gained 2.52 percent and industrials closed up 1.93 percent.
Leasing shares firmed 1.81 percent up and small-caps gained 1.12 percent. Insurance shares ended 0.92 higher.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted at 969.00-1007.00. Shares of OTE telecom the underlying, ended 80 drachmas higher at 5,750.

The recently launched ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $41.86-$43.56. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The recently issued ING Baring Financial Products American- style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted at 1,602-1,781 drachmas.
The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The Morgan Stanley Hellenic Blue Chip Warrant, which has a strike price of 100 marks, was quoted at 11,666-12,279 drachmas. --Margarita Sotiropoulou, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
